subject: Scheduling maintenance & rollback plan for Private deployment (version pinning)
messages:
From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@acmepay.com>
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Upgrading Redwood Private in our VPC - scheduling

Hi Priya,

We're preparing to upgrade our Redwood Private deployment from 1.4.1 to 1.4.2. Security is requesting a clearly documented maintenance window, pinned versions during the window, and a tested rollback plan for audit purposes (SOC 2). Can you propose a maintenance window next week (PST preferred) and confirm: 1) whether version pinning will prevent urgent hotfixes, 2) if any KV-cache or config migrations are required, and 3) whether you can run a staged canary so we can validate quality before full cutover?

Also please include any preflight checks you expect us to run on our side and the exact commands for rollback (for our runbook). We need to attach this to our change record.

Thanks,
Alice Monroe
Lead DevOps, Acme Payments
alice.monroe@acmepay.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@acmepay.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-08T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Upgrading Redwood Private in our VPC - scheduling

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear ask. We can absolutely support a pinned, auditable upgrade with a staged canary and documented rollback. Proposed plan (high level):

- Proposed maintenance window: 2027-04-11 02:00–04:00 UTC (2027-04-10 19:00–21:00 PDT). If PST evening is preferred we can shift earlier; please confirm.
- Version pinning: during the window our control plane will pin the deployment images to 1.4.2. Pinning prevents automatic roll-forward but does not block emergency patching — we can perform emergency hotfixes by temporarily unpinning with an approval step (documented in the runbook).
- Canary strategy: roll 10% of replicas first (metrics gating below). If canary passes, roll remaining nodes in 3 waves.
- KV/cache: no schema migration; we will snapshot KV stores and warm caches during canary. We will not invalidate caches unless we detect correctness issues.
- Rollback: automated rollback hook exists in the runbook: revert to 1.4.1 image, restore previous KV snapshot, and redeploy route weights.
- Preflight checks for Acme: ensure bastion access to jump host is enabled, provide one sudo-capable user, confirm snapshot schedule is on (we will take an additional snapshot).

Attachments: runbook_20270411.pdf (detailed steps), config_delta_1.4.2.patch (diff of configs), access-sheet.csv (template to fill with bastion key fingerprints).

I'll loop Karthik and Lauren to confirm the low-level rollback commands and SLIs we will gate on. Once we have internal sign-off I'll post the runbook and Jira SUP-3456 with the final steps.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Eng - Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-09T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Upgrading Redwood Private in our VPC - scheduling

Priya / Lauren — quick tech note to include in the runbook:

- Preflight (automated): healthcheck cluster (svc: /health), verify KV snapshot TTL, confirm disk usage < 70%, validate network ACLs allow outbound to S3 (for images) and to our metrics endpoint. Command snippets included below.
- Canary rollout: use rolling update with maxUnavailable=0, maxSurge=1 (k8s-style) to keep capacity. Start with 1/10 nodes on canary tag image: redwood/private:1.4.2-canary. After 20 minutes, run the canary smoke tests (latency p99 < 200ms, error rate < 0.5%, embed pipeline throughput within 10% of baseline).
- Metrics gating: p50/p95/p99, error-rate, request queue length, and token-per-second must meet thresholds. We'll automate gating via Prometheus alert rule that flips to pass/fail for the orchestration script.
- Rollback actions (fast path):
  1) Revert image tag to 1.4.1 (or restore from pinned artifact).
  2) Run "redwoodctl restore-kv --snapshot <id>" (we'll snapshot right before canary).
  3) Re-route traffic weight to previous variant and monitor for 15 minutes.
- Postmortem hooks: capture logs for last 1 hour via our collection agent and snapshot audit logs for SOC2 evidence.

No DB migrations expected. Edge case: if config_delta introduces feature flags, ensure flags default to off.

I'll add the exact command snippets into runbook_20270411.pdf before sending.

-karthik

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@acmepay.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-10T17:58:00-07:00
Subject: Final runbook + Jira SUP-3456 link — please confirm window

Hi Alice — attaching the final runbook and config diff (also pushed to SUP-3456). Summary highlights:

- Window: 2027-04-11 02:00–04:00 UTC (we'll start canary at 02:10).
- Gate thresholds: p99 latency < 250ms, 5m error rate < 0.5%, embedding QPS within 15% of baseline.
- Rollback command (fast): "redwoodctl release rollback --deployment acme-prod --to 1.4.1 --snapshot <id>". Full steps are in runbook_20270411.pdf.
- Required from Acme: populated access-sheet.csv (attached) with bastion key fingerprint and confirmation that the jump host user can sudo for our ops user. Please upload the filled sheet to the shared GDrive folder or reply with the fingerprint before 2027-04-11 00:00 UTC.
- Audit evidence: we'll attach post-deploy logs and the snapshot id to the Jira ticket SUP-3456. Link: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/SUP-3456

If that window works I'll mark the ticket "approved" and start the orchestration (we'll also take the preflight snapshot at T-30m). If you want PST evening instead, propose a 2-hour shift and we'll accommodate.

Thanks — Priya

Attachments:
- runbook_20270411.pdf (step-by-step with commands & approvals)
- config_delta_1.4.2.patch
- access-sheet.csv (please fill)

From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@acmepay.com>
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: Infra Team <infra@acmepay.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T03:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Final runbook + Jira SUP-3456 link — please confirm window

Hi Priya — window confirmed. We've uploaded the completed access-sheet.csv to the Drive folder and opened inbound bastion access for redwood-ops (fingerprint matches). Proceed with the canary at 02:10 UTC. We'll be standing by on the change call.

Thanks,
Alice
notes: Runbook includes step-by-step canary, metrics gating, and automated rollback hooks; customer to provide bastion access before window. Post-deploy artifacts will be attached to SUP-3456 for SOC2 evidence.
